items.q: To record the parasternal long axis view, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The parasternal long axis view is obtained from the left sternal edge at the third or fourth space, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the parasternal long axis view is correctly cut?
o: Left ventricle with septum, mitral valve, aortic root and left atrium
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when left ventricle with septum, mitral valve, aortic root and left atrium is clearly seen, because descending aorta in cross section behind the left atrium confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the parasternal short axis view at aortic level, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The parasternal short axis view at aortic level is obtained from the left sternal edge at the third space tilted to the base, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the parasternal short axis view at aortic level is correctly cut?
o: Aortic valve with three cusps closing in the middle
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when aortic valve with three cusps closing in the middle is clearly seen, because right ventricular outflow tract in front with the pulmonary valve confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the parasternal short axis view at mitral level, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The parasternal short axis view at mitral level is obtained from the left sternal edge mid sweep, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the parasternal short axis view at mitral level is correctly cut?
o: Mitral valve with anterior and posterior leaflets opening like a fish mouth
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when mitral valve with anterior and posterior leaflets opening like a fish mouth is clearly seen, because no papillary muscle in the same cut confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the parasternal short axis view at papillary muscle level, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The parasternal short axis view at papillary muscle level is obtained from the left sternal edge at the fourth space, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the parasternal short axis view at papillary muscle level is correctly cut?
o: Two papillary muscles placed nearly opposite each other
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when two papillary muscles placed nearly opposite each other is clearly seen, because circular left ventricular cavity in the middle confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the apical four chamber view, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The apical four chamber view is obtained from the cardiac apex with the marker to the left, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the apical four chamber view is correctly cut?
o: Four chambers with the septa nearly vertical on screen
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when four chambers with the septa nearly vertical on screen is clearly seen, because true apex showing the thinnest point of the left ventricle confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the apical five chamber view, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The apical five chamber view is obtained from the cardiac apex tilted forward from the four chamber cut, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the apical five chamber view is correctly cut?
o: Aortic valve with the left ventricular outflow tract below it
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when aortic valve with the left ventricular outflow tract below it is clearly seen, because anterior angulation that opens the outflow below the mitral plane confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the apical two chamber view, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The apical two chamber view is obtained from the cardiac apex rotated about 60 degrees from the four chamber cut, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the apical two chamber view is correctly cut?
o: Anterior and inferior walls with no septum on screen
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when anterior and inferior walls with no septum on screen is clearly seen, because left atrial appendage beside the left atrium confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the apical three chamber view, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The apical three chamber view is obtained from the cardiac apex rotated further to an apical long axis cut, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the apical three chamber view is correctly cut?
o: Aortic valve with the outflow tract seen from the apex
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when aortic valve with the outflow tract seen from the apex is clearly seen, because anteroseptal and inferolateral walls around the cavity confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the subcostal four chamber view, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The subcostal four chamber view is obtained from the subxiphoid window pushing up under the ribs, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the subcostal four chamber view is correctly cut?
o: Four chambers seen through the liver window
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when four chambers seen through the liver window is clearly seen, because interatrial septum well placed for shunt checks confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the subcostal inferior vena cava view, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The subcostal inferior vena cava view is obtained from the subxiphoid window rotated to the long axis of the vein, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the subcostal inferior vena cava view is correctly cut?
o: Inferior vena cava entering the right atrium
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when inferior vena cava entering the right atrium is clearly seen, because hepatic vein joining the cava above the liver confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the suprasternal arch view, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The suprasternal arch view is obtained from the sternal notch with the marker pointing up, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the suprasternal arch view is correctly cut?
o: Aortic arch with three head and neck branches
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when aortic arch with three head and neck branches is clearly seen, because right pulmonary artery crossing below the arch confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the right ventricular inflow view, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The right ventricular inflow view is obtained from the left sternal edge with anterior tilt, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the right ventricular inflow view is correctly cut?
o: Tricuspid valve with right atrium and right ventricle
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when tricuspid valve with right atrium and right ventricle is clearly seen, because anterior and septal leaflets of the tricuspid valve confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the parasternal right ventricular outflow view, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The parasternal right ventricular outflow view is obtained from the left sternal edge with superior tilt, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the parasternal right ventricular outflow view is correctly cut?
o: Pulmonary valve with the main pulmonary artery
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when pulmonary valve with the main pulmonary artery is clearly seen, because bifurcation into left and right pulmonary arteries confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: To record the subcostal short axis view, which window is the best starting point?
items.exp: The subcostal short axis view is obtained from the subxiphoid window swept to cross section, so the other windows give the wrong plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on standard views and windows.

items.q: Which finding tells you the subcostal short axis view is correctly cut?
o: Left ventricle in cross section at papillary level
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
items.exp: Accept the view only when left ventricle in cross section at papillary level is clearly seen, because right ventricle wrapping in front of the circle confirms the true plane. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: The left ventricle looks rounded with a short length in the apical four chamber view. What is wrong and how do you correct it?
o: Tilt to the base to open the outflow
Move the probe to the true apex to gain the longest cavity
Press harder to squeeze the ribs apart
Raise gain to brighten the apex
items.exp: A rounded short cavity means foreshortening, so the probe is off the apex and volumes will read small. Move to the true apex for the longest length. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on avoiding foreshortening.

items.q: In the parasternal long axis view a gap appears in the upper septum in one frame. What should you suspect first?
o: Off axis dropout that vanishes in a true perpendicular cut
A vegetation on the aortic valve
items.exp: Septal dropout from an off axis cut mimics a defect, so confirm in a perpendicular plane with colour before calling it real. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on common artefacts.

items.q: Rib shadow hides the lateral wall. What is the best first move?
o: Freeze and measure through the shadow
Slide the probe to sit between the ribs
items.exp: Rib blocks sound fully, so no knob restores the hidden wall and the window must move between the ribs. Guideline: BSE minimum dataset, section on acoustic windows.

items.q: The near field is full of bright clutter in the parasternal view. What helps most?
o: Lower near gain with the time gain controls
items.exp: Near field clutter comes from excess near gain, so turning down the near time gain sliders clears it while keeping far detail. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on image optimisation.

items.q: The aortic valve shows only two cusps in short axis. What is the likely cause?
o: An oblique cut through the valve plane
items.exp: An oblique cut can hide one cusp, so sweep through the full valve level before labelling the valve bicuspid. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on parasternal short axis views.

items.q: The apical four chamber view shows five chambers with an aorta below the mitral plane. Which view is this?
items.exp: Anterior tilt from the four chamber plane opens the outflow tract with the aortic valve, which defines the five chamber view. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on apical views.

items.q: The inferior vena cava does not collapse on sniffing during the subcostal check. What does the technique require?
o: Measuring during quiet tidal rest only
A short sharp sniff with the sample in the long axis of the vein
items.exp: A sharp sniff drops intrathoracic pressure briefly, and the long axis cut keeps the vein in plane so collapse can be judged fairly. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on inferior vena cava and right atrial pressure.

items.q: The suprasternal view shows the arch but no branches. What should you do?
o: Fan slightly to bring the head and neck branches into plane
Press the probe deeper into the notch
items.exp: The three branches leave the arch in a slightly different plane, so gentle fanning reveals them without losing the arch. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on suprasternal views.

items.q: A bright mobile mass at the apex appears only in one apical cut. What should you suspect?
o: A vegetation on the mitral valve
Near field artefact or trabeculation rather than true thrombus
A myxoma of the left ventricle
items.exp: Trabeculation and near field artefact vanish in other planes, while true thrombus persists in two planes beside a wall motion defect. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on apical views and artefacts.

items.q: Depth is set so the heart fills only half the sector. What is the cost?
o: Wasted lines and a lower frame rate with a small image
items.exp: Excess depth spends scan lines below the heart, so the image stays small and the frame rate falls for no gain. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on image optimisation.

items.q: The marker dot points the wrong way and left looks like right on screen. What is the rule?
o: Always point the marker to the head
Always point the marker to the feet
The marker side does not matter
Keep the marker toward the reference stated for that window
items.exp: Each window has a stated marker direction, and keeping it makes orientation and wall labelling consistent. Guideline: BSE minimum dataset, section on standard orientation.

items.q: The mitral leaflets look thick and bright only at the base of the sweep. What is happening?
o: The cut is too basal so normal tissue reads thick
items.exp: A basal cut slices leaflets obliquely and makes them look thick, so centre the valve at mid sweep before judging thickness. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on parasternal short axis views.
